correctness.rationale: For a singleton successor relation the strong-disagreement bundle is exactly the linear map T(x)(w)=x(f(w))+x(g(w)) over F2. The constant-one vector is a nonzero kernel element, so rank T<=n-1. The eventual invertible restriction S to the stable image has exact order 2^r. In characteristic two, N=S+I has N^(2^r)=0 and N^(2^(r-1)) nonzero, giving stable-image dimension >=2^(r-1)+1 and n>=2^(r-1)+2. Explicit idempotent retractions on 0..m, m=2^(r-1)+1, realize T|U=I+N with a single nilpotent shift of length m and exact order 2^r. Since im T=U, the period starts after the first application. All ranks and boundary cases are included; the checker performs actual finite support checks from packaged checker.py, without asserting finite enumeration proves the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly determines the smallest carrier on which iterated two-agent strong disagreement can have each dyadic eventual period, for all r>=1, across the entire functional KD45 class. It exposes unbounded periodic modal nesting despite both constituent single-agent modalities being idempotent and yields pairwise inequivalence of all positive iterates. This is a motivated sharp finite-model expressivity threshold, not a routine enumeration or an arbitrary slice.
